newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Saurer sees EBIT up, may repay capital.
newsitem.headline: Saurer sees EBIT up, may repay capital.

text.p: Swiss textile machinery and automobile component maker Saurer AG said that its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) was likely to grow by significantly more than 10 percent in 1997.
Chairman Ernst Thomke, speaking at the company's year-end news briefing, also said that it was possible the company could consider a further capital repayment.
Saurer has alrady proposed paying back shareholders 15 Swiss francs per share.
The payback is in lieu of a dividend on 1996 results.
Saurer posted a 51 million Swiss franc net profit for 1996 versus a 75 million franc loss in 1995.
Thomke also expected further growth in China and India.
Chief finance officer Heinrich Fischer said that Saurer was also hoping to bring its components group on the stock exchange in two to three years.
The components group is to be transfered to BB Industrie Holding AG (BBI), which holds 32 percent of Saurer, providing a planned takeover of BB is finalised.
Saurer said in April it had launched a takeover offer to shareholders for BB, which was supported by BB.
